claims: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission marked a safe return for the crew after their trip around the moon.
Footage of the reentry, parachute deployment, and splashdown is available from NASA, PBS, and major news outlets like WBAL-TV.
NASA YouTube Channel features the complete live coverage, including atmospheric entry, heat shield performance, and capsule splashdown.
NBC News provides clips of the parachute deployment and splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
BBC News covers the separation, blackout period, and final splashdown.
PBS Newshour offers video coverage of the crew returning to Earth.
The Orion capsule splashed down west of San Diego around 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Orion capsule splashdown concluded a 10-day mission.
Recovery teams immediately began securing the capsule and retrieving the crew.
The securing of the capsule and retrieving of the crew was captured in live video feeds.
